summary: Intermittent request timeouts and tail-latency spikes for very large context + high max_tokens generations
description: Issue summary: Customer reports intermittent 504/timeout responses and long tail-latency for inference requests that include a very large historical context (50k+ input tokens) combined with high max_tokens for generation (20k+). Impact: Search assistant experiences ~15% request failure rate during batch windows; user-facing sessions show stalls and failed completions. Environment: Dedicated cluster serving LexiSearch workloads in us-east with reserved GPU pool (p4d-like instances) and custom batching settings (max_batch_tokens=131072, aggressive batching on). Observed behavior: Elevated 95/99th percentile latency and a subset of requests hitting 504 gateway timeouts. No consistent model crash; processes remain up but CPU and host-side memory spike. Expected behavior: Requests that fit configured hard limits should complete or stream partial output instead of timing out.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use dedicated tenant for LexiSearch in prod/us-east.
2) Construct a request with ~55k tokens of context (concatenated conversation + indexed snippets) and set max_tokens to 22k.
3) Send 8 concurrent requests to the same model endpoint with default priority and streaming=false.
4) Observe response times and HTTP status codes from the gateway and runtime.
5) Alternately reproduce by increasing batch traffic from other tenants to force larger consolidate batches on the serving runtime.

comments: [2026-03-10] Support - Ava Chen: Customer reported recurring 504s in the afternoon traffic window. They have a dedicated cluster; issue affects only very long-context requests with large generation length. Customer notices spikes happen when other jobs are concurrently running high-token batches.

[2026-03-10] Eng Triage - Miguel Torres: Confirmed reproducer locally using a trimmed context. Observed similar tail latency and memory pressure on the host. Opening investigation; suspect batching heuristics + KV merge path causing large host-side copies.

[2026-03-11] SRE - Lina Park: Collected perf profiles for host-3 and runtime traces. Heap growth correlates to KV cache merge during request scheduling. Noted increased mutex contention in batch assembly code path.

[2026-03-12] Customer - Rajesh Kumar (LexiSearch): Provided exact prompt files and confirmed that reducing max_tokens to 4k eliminates failures but user experience is degraded. Asking about short-term mitigation while Redwood patches runtime.

[2026-03-13] Eng - Miguel Torres: Implemented a conservative workaround on staging: reduce max_batch_tokens per worker and enable early streaming flush; reproducer failure rate dropped from 18% -> 1.2% in stress test. Preparing hotfix for production.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Aggressive batching can combine many long-context requests into a single huge token batch, causing host memory spikes and long KV merge times leading to gateway timeouts.
Hypothesis 2: The KV-cache merge code path does an O(n) copy for each request that doesn't fit preallocated buffers; at large sequence lengths this becomes a dominant contributor to tail latency.
Evidence: Profiling shows long blocking sections in batch-assembly mutex and repeated allocations (~200MB per request) during merge. Host-level metrics show high CPU and I/O wait during the spikes.

Reproducer: Running 8 concurrent synthetic requests with 55k context + 22k generation reproduces 504s in ~20% of runs when max_batch_tokens is set to 131072; lowering to 65536 reduced failures to <2%.

Cross-references: Related to internal note INT-4218 where we observed similar KV merge slowness for long prefix inference but with different model families; appears to be systemic to the runtime's merging heuristics.
resolution_notes: Workarounds applied: 1) Temporarily set soft limit on per-worker max_batch_tokens for the customer's dedicated pool to 65536. 2) Enabled early streaming for large requests so partial tokens are returned and gateway timeouts are less likely. 3) Advised customer to lower max_tokens to <=10k where feasible.

Permanent fix: Engineering to land a runtime patch that 1) preallocates KV merge buffers for requests exceeding threshold, 2) optimizes batch-assembly to avoid per-request large copies, and 3) introduces a smarter batch-splitting heuristic for long-sequence requests.
Rollout plan: Hotfix v1.3.9-rc -> canary on dedicated pools (us-east host-2) -> expand to remaining nodes after 24h monitoring. Target prod rollout: 2026-03-16 if metrics stable.
Customer communication: CS to notify LexiSearch of temporary mitigation and proposed rollout schedule. Follow-up call scheduled 2026-03-14 14:00 ET.
Postmortem action items: Create benchmark to exercise long-context + high-gen combinations (owner: Performance team). Add regression test in CI for KV merge path (owner: Serving runtime).
Status: In Progress - hotfix in QA.
